title: 2: Dimension Reduction
text:
This reading:

build the intuition for thinking about “dimensions” of data
introduce some key goals and methods that researchers use, and how these differ in relation to finding and using dimensions of data

title: 2: Dimension Reduction
text:
naive scale scores
e.g., rowMeans
Goal: pragmatic. i want 1 thing to use in some other setting (e.g., in a further analysis, or in a clinical setting)

how do we find the dimensions?

there’s only one

how many dimensions should we retain?

there’s only one

how does each dimension relate back to the original measured variables?

equally

title: 2: Dimension Reduction
text:
PCA
Goal: pragmatic. i need fewer things for use in a subsequent analysis but don’t want to lose too much variability.

how do we find the dimensions?

set of orthogonal (i.e., perpendicular3) dimensions that sequentially capture most variability

how many dimensions should we retain?

pragmatic: defined by either the number of dimensions we want, or the proportion of variability we want to retain

how does each dimension relate back to the original measured variables?

examine correlations between dimensions and variables
somewhat irrelevant for ‘pure’ PCA, where we are agnostic/don’t care about what the dimensions are.

title: 2: Dimension Reduction
text:
EFA
Goal: scale development. i want to make a measure of construct X / I want to explore if/how many underlying dimensions there are to this measure.

how do we find the dimensions?

estimation
models with different numbers of (possibly correlated) latent dimensions are compared

how many dimensions should we retain?

the model that best explains our observed relationships between variables
“best explains” = a theoretical question as much as a numerical one!


how does each dimension relate back to the original measured variables?

examine “loadings” between dimensions and variables

title: 2: Dimension Reduction
text:
CFA
Goal: theory testing. I have a theoretical model of how these variables relate to these constructs. I want to test how well that model is reflected in these data

how do we find the dimensions?

we define them

how many dimensions should we retain?

irrelevant, the dimensions are pre-defined

how does each dimension relate back to the original measured variables?

pre-defined

title: 1: Data Wrangling for Questionnaires
text:
Questionnaire data often comes to us in ‘wide’ format, which is often how we want it for many of the analytical methods we use with questionnaire data. However, working with data in the wide format comes with some specific challenges that generally arise because we have lots and lots of variables.
Below we will walk through some of the common ways we want to wrangle and clean questionnaire data.
